newsitem.title: UK: Shield Diagnostics soar after clinical study.
newsitem.headline: Shield Diagnostics soar after clinical study.

text.p: Shares in Shield Diagnostics Group Plc were up 60p to 710p by 1015 GMT after hitting a high of 745p after the company said in a statement that clinical trials showed a link between increased levels of a blood clotting agent, known as AFT, and heart attacks.
"The market has been waiting for this news for months," one market maker said. "We've seen an initial spike but we might see some profit-taking now."

Shield has been developing a diagnostic kit which it says can show the presence of AFT and has been hoping studies would show there is a link between the clotting agent and a propensity to heart attacks.
After closing at 175p a share on January 31, Shield shares hit a 12-month high of 928p on March 14 but the share came off the top as doubts surfaced about AFT studies.
But the company said in a statement on Monday that clinical studies pointed toward AFT becoming a "significant tool" for clinicians to use in assessing cardiovascular risk.
"The potential of AFT as a risk marker for coronary artery disease and heart attack was clear," the company said in a statement.
